about: The tools and the instructions of the Nuclear MCP server.

rows.title: `api_inspect` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Fetches a public API's url and answers the shape of its JSON (keys, types, nested objects, a paged answer).
body: Fetches a public API's url and answers the shape of its JSON (keys, types, nested objects, a paged answer). With project, component and name it also shows the files generate_resource would write from it.

rows.title: `developer_code` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Ask the local developer (a 3B model with the graph) for ONE .nuc file, outside a developer_task run (a quick piece, a rewrite of one file).
body: Ask the local developer (a 3B model with the graph) for ONE .nuc file, outside a developer_task run (a quick piece, a rewrite of one file). A short, complete order: the path, the kind, every name and signature it must use and the platform (backend, mobile, web; it writes only Nuclear). With project (the project's folder) it reads by itself the files that declare the names the task writes; otherwise paste them in context. It checks its answer with the compiler, repairs it, holds it to the task's own words and returns it; it does not write the file.

rows.title: `developer_retry` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: A developer_task run that failed, again from the step that failed (every step that passed is kept), or the whole of from_stage (plan, test, code, verify, security, artifacts, deploy), the stages before it kept.
body: A developer_task run that failed, again from the step that failed (every step that passed is kept), or the whole of from_stage (plan, test, code, verify, security, artifacts, deploy), the stages before it kept. Read the journal's "Why it failed" first: retry when the failure was passing (a service down) or after you fixed its cause. Answers the journal again.

rows.title: `developer_review` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: LAST STEP: record your review of a developer_task run: what you corrected and why (notes), and the project paths of the files you corrected.
body: LAST STEP: record your review of a developer_task run: what you corrected and why (notes), and the project paths of the files you corrected. Appends it to the run's journal and keeps each corrected file, with its task, in the graph's examples so the local developer writes it right next time.

rows.title: `developer_security` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Ask the local security reviewer for the findings of a piece of code.
body: Ask the local security reviewer for the findings of a piece of code.

rows.title: `developer_task` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: FIRST STEP of every task that writes .nuc: the local Nuclear Developer does the whole task in the project folder (plan, tests first, code, verification, security, artifacts) and documents it.
body: FIRST STEP of every task that writes .nuc: the local Nuclear Developer does the whole task in the project folder (plan, tests first, code, verification, security, artifacts) and documents it. Give the description and one acceptance criterion per item; use_case: feature, bug, refactor, test. Answers the run's journal (every step, the files written, what is left for you); then validate and correct, and call developer_review.

rows.title: `developer_test` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Ask the local tester for the Nuclear tests (`tests` kind) of a piece of code.
body: Ask the local tester for the Nuclear tests (`tests` kind) of a piece of code.

rows.title: `dragonfly` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: A dragonfly command in a project folder: new, build, install, test, check, analyze, make (g), migrate, add, explain.
body: A dragonfly command in a project folder: new, build, install, test, check, analyze, make (g), migrate, add, explain. Example: command="make", args=["component", "orders"].

rows.title: `generate_component` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: A new component of the project with its facade (appcomponent).
body: A new component of the project with its facade (appcomponent).

rows.title: `generate_resource` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The finished, compiling code of a resource: its models, the repository, one use case per action, the facade's aliases, the controller (backend) or, with screen, a screen with its state manager (mobile, web), and the tests.
body: The finished, compiling code of a resource: its models, the repository, one use case per action, the facade's aliases, the controller (backend) or, with screen, a screen with its state manager (mobile, web), and the tests. The fields: from_json (an example answer of the API: a url, which also gives the API, or a file), from_spec (a spec.md: its example answer or its Key | Type table, and its `GET <url>` line), or fields ("id:int name:string origin:Origin?"). source: "rest:<base url>", "rest" or "db" (backend only). actions: of list, get, search, create, update, delete (default: list and get for an API, the rest for a database). dry_run shows the files without writing them. Nothing is overwritten; a name declared elsewhere stops it.

rows.title: `generate_screen` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: A screen of a mobile or web project with its state manager and state model, for a view that is not a list of a resource (generate_resource with screen writes those).
body: A screen of a mobile or web project with its state manager and state model, for a view that is not a list of a resource (generate_resource with screen writes those).

rows.title: `generate_usecase` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: A use case wired into its component: its alias in the facade and, with route (backend), its route in the controller of the route's prefix ("POST orders/{id}/cancel": a {name} is a parameter of the use case; the controller is created when missing).
body: A use case wired into its component: its alias in the facade and, with route (backend), its route in the controller of the route's prefix ("POST orders/{id}/cancel": a {name} is a parameter of the use case; the controller is created when missing). With calls ("OrderRepository.pending": a method that repository declares) the use case is written too, because it only calls that method. Without calls the use case must already be in the project: one with rules of its own is written first (developer_task, or by hand), then this wires it. dry_run shows the files without writing them.

rows.title: `graph_card` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: One row of the graph by its id, with what it links to: error:N0114 (a diagnostic), kind:backend.usecase, decorator:backend.get, tool:dragonfly.gen.resource, mcp:generate_resource, lib:string, platform:mobile, layout:web, playbook:<name>, concept:<name>.
body: One row of the graph by its id, with what it links to: error:N0114 (a diagnostic), kind:backend.usecase, decorator:backend.get, tool:dragonfly.gen.resource, mcp:generate_resource, lib:string, platform:mobile, layout:web, playbook:<name>, concept:<name>.

rows.title: `graph_prompt` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The validated prompt of a use case: feature, refactor, bug, docs, diagram, test, security, piece, plan.
body: The validated prompt of a use case: feature, refactor, bug, docs, diagram, test, security, piece, plan.

rows.title: `graph_remember` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Keep a decision, a name or a solved example (collection examples: the task, then the validated .nuc) so the local developer and later sessions find it.
body: Keep a decision, a name or a solved example (collection examples: the task, then the validated .nuc) so the local developer and later sessions find it.

rows.title: `graph_search` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Search the Nuclear Smart Graph, by meaning and by exact name (a diagnostic code, a command, a kind).
body: Search the Nuclear Smart Graph, by meaning and by exact name (a diagnostic code, a command, a kind). shelf: concepts (what it is, why, how it works), language (how it is written in Nuclear), platforms (kinds, decorators, layout, plugins), tools (CLI commands, MCP tools, HTTP routes, generators, agents), errors (diagnostics, failures and their fixes), capabilities (what can and cannot be done, limits), playbooks (procedures, roles, skills), examples (validated Nuclear), docs (the long documents: dialects, ADRs, context, status), memory (what agents kept about projects); several separated by commas; "" searches every shelf. platform: backend, mobile, web. kind: a kind's rows (usecase, repository...). type: a row type (diagnostic, kind, cli, playbook...). Each card comes with the rows it links to.

rows.title: `graph_strategy` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Which kind of request this is (a whole system, a component, a resource, one screen, a use case, a rename, a failing test, a question...) and the plan of that kind, step by step with the tool of each step.
body: Which kind of request this is (a whole system, a component, a resource, one screen, a use case, a rename, a failing test, a question...) and the plan of that kind, step by step with the tool of each step. Call it first, with the user's request in their own words, and follow the plan it answers. platform: backend, mobile or web.

rows.title: `nuclear_brief` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The short sheet of Nuclear and a platform (backend, mobile, web), or a dialect: read it before writing .nuc.
body: The short sheet of Nuclear and a platform (backend, mobile, web), or a dialect: read it before writing .nuc.

rows.title: `nuclear_build` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: What a piece of Nuclear becomes in the dialect's language (Python, TypeScript, Dart).
body: What a piece of Nuclear becomes in the dialect's language (Python, TypeScript, Dart).

rows.title: `nuclear_check` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Errors of a piece of Nuclear (code) or of a whole project (path of its folder): `ok` or one line per error with its fix.
body: Errors of a piece of Nuclear (code) or of a whole project (path of its folder): `ok` or one line per error with its fix.

rows.title: `nuclear_defs` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: A declaration of the type definitions (a class or Class.member of a library the dialect uses).
body: A declaration of the type definitions (a class or Class.member of a library the dialect uses).

rows.title: `nuclear_fmt` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The piece of Nuclear in the canonical layout.
body: The piece of Nuclear in the canonical layout.

rows.title: `nuclear_help` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Documentation of a kind, decorator, header word (with dialect), a topic or a command.
body: Documentation of a kind, decorator, header word (with dialect), a topic or a command.

rows.title: `project_inspect` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: What a Dragonfly project has: its platform and dialect, its components with their declarations by kind, and the generators of its platform.
body: What a Dragonfly project has: its platform and dialect, its components with their declarations by kind, and the generators of its platform. Call it before generating or writing, so nothing is declared twice.

rows.title: The Nuclear MCP server: its tools and how a client must work with them
rows.summary: `nuclear-graph mcp` speaks the Model Context Protocol over stdio and gives an AI client 26 tools: the Smart Graph, the compiler, the dragonfly commands, the generators, the internet and the local developer.
body: NuclearLang and Dragonfly. The generators write the standard code, the local Nuclear Developer writes what is left; you lead, validate and correct. For any request, first call graph_strategy with the user's own words: it answers which kind of request it is (a whole system, one screen, a rename, a failing test...) and the plan of that kind; follow that plan. For a feature: 0) project_inspect the project; for every resource the spec names (a model and what is done with it: list, get, search, create, update, delete), call generate_resource. Its fields come from the API's answer (from_json with the url or a file: api_inspect shows its shape first), from the spec (from_spec: its example answer or its Key | Type table) or from fields; when neither the spec nor the API gives them, look up the API's documentation with web_search and web_read, and if it is still unclear ask the user, never guess. A use case that only calls a repository method is generate_usecase with calls. Then give developer_task only what the generators did not write (a use case with its own rules, a view's details), and wire each use case it wrote with generate_usecase (its alias in the facade, its route). For any task that writes or changes .nuc (a feature, a bug, a refactor, tests): 1) call developer_task first with the project folder, a title, the description and the acceptance criteria: the local agents plan, write the tests first, write the code, run the tests and the security review, and document everything they did in a journal it returns; 2) read the journal, then validate: nuclear_check of the project must say ok and dragonfly test must pass; 3) correct only what failed or is wrong, never rewrite what passed; before writing .nuc read nuclear_brief(<platform>: backend, mobile or web) and search the graph instead of guessing; If the run failed, read its 'Why it failed' (the local diagnoser): when the cause was passing or you fixed it, call developer_retry instead of starting again. 4) call developer_review with the run, what you corrected and why, and the corrected files, so the journal keeps your review and the local developer learns from it. Write the code yourself only when developer_task cannot run (the local developer is not running) and say so.

rows.title: `web_read` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The text of a public page (an API's documentation), without its code blocks.
body: The text of a public page (an API's documentation), without its code blocks.

rows.title: `web_search` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Searches the internet (e.g.
body: Searches the internet (e.g. an API's documentation: "rick and morty api character schema") and answers the first results with the text of their first pages.
